AgentBox gives each AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or just a shell) its own Linux machine: a worktree on its own branch, Docker, a browser you can watch and take over, an Android emulator for mobile apps, and a place for the screenshots, recordings and test reports that show its work. Several agents work on the same project at once without getting in each other's way.

**AgentBox now ships with a README, a contributing guide, and issue and pull request templates.** **A project can be limited to some of your Claude accounts**, so its agents never land on the ones it shouldn't bill. **You choose each chat's context window**, 200k or the model's whole 1M, in the project's chat, in an agent's chat, and when an agent is made. **The project's chat is terse, and does the routine follow-through itself**, such as retiring merged agents and starting the obvious next one, instead of asking about each step. Linux on x86_64.

## Downloads

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `AgentBox-0.16.0-x86_64.AppImage` | The desktop app, with the `agentbox` command-line tool inside — runs on any Linux distribution |
| `AgentBox-0.16.0-amd64.deb` | The desktop app, for Debian and Ubuntu (`sudo apt install ./AgentBox-0.16.0-amd64.deb`) |
| `AgentBox-0.16.0-x64.pacman` | The desktop app, for Arch and its derivatives (`sudo pacman -U AgentBox-0.16.0-x64.pacman`) |
| `agentbox-0.16.0-linux-amd64` | The command-line tool and daemon alone, for servers and scripts |
| `SHA256SUMS` | Checksums: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` |

## Install

```bash
chmod +x AgentBox-0.16.0-x86_64.AppImage
./AgentBox-0.16.0-x86_64.AppImage
```

Or, on Debian/Ubuntu, `sudo apt install ./AgentBox-0.16.0-amd64.deb`; on Arch, `sudo pacman -U AgentBox-0.16.0-x64.pacman`. Both install a launcher alongside the app.

On a new machine, open **Settings** in the app and follow its steps, as described in the README's [Set up](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/blob/v0.16.0/README.md#set-up). Without the app: `install -m 0755 agentbox-0.16.0-linux-amd64 ~/.local/bin/agentbox`, then the terminal steps in the same section.

### Upgrading from 0.15.0

Replace the AppImage (or install the new .deb/.pacman over the old one) and open it: it restarts the daemon with the new version once no job is running. Existing projects and agents keep working. **The base image hasn't changed** (it is still `2026.09.22.1`), so Setup won't ask you to rebuild it. Four things change, though:

- **One migration adds `claude_accounts` to every project, empty.** An empty list allows every account, so every existing project can still use every account until you set a list.
- **Existing project chats get the new, terse brief.** The brief is rewritten before every turn, so the chat picks it up when its session next starts. The autonomy setting you chose isn't changed, but **`ask` now means something different**: a project on `ask`, which is still the default, now does routine follow-through without asking first. That means retiring merged agents, answering agents, starting the obvious next agent and getting problems it found fixed. It still asks about product decisions and anything costly or irreversible. Neither setting throws away unpushed work without saying so, pushes to main, merges, releases or tags unless you ask, and both warn before big spend.
- **A stored `opus[1m]` now reads as `opus`, and compacts where it always did.** `opus[1m]` is no longer on the model list, and the default for new agents is plain `opus`. Every agent, chat and setting that stored `opus[1m]` before this release keeps running on Opus and keeps compacting at your installation's compact window, 200k by default. None of them moves to 1M unless you choose it.
- **Agents that already hold an account keep it**, even if you then leave that account out of the project's list: its token is already on the agent's machine. The list only affects new choices.

## What's new

### AgentBox is open source

- **MIT license.** `LICENSE` is in the repository, and the .deb and .pacman now say `License: MIT`.
- **A README** with a tour of the features, screenshots of the real app, install and setup, a quick start, how it works, and the requirements and limitations. **CONTRIBUTING.md** explains how to build it, run it and test it, the project's conventions, and how pull requests and CI work. There are issue forms for bugs and features, and a pull request template.
- **The implementation write-ups and decision records are no longer in the repository.** Each change's reasoning is in its pull request's description and in comments in the code.

### Limit which Claude accounts a project may use

- **Each project can have a list of allowed accounts**, for example `work` and `client` but never `personal`. An empty list allows every account.
- **In the app:** the project's page has an **Allowed accounts** row under its Claude account, with one toggle per account. The project's own account is locked on. The New agent dialog offers only the allowed accounts.
- **From the terminal:**
  ```bash
  agentbox claude-account myapp --allow work,client   # only these two
  agentbox claude-account myapp --allow-add spare     # add one
  agentbox claude-account myapp --allow-remove client # remove one
  agentbox claude-account myapp --allow-all           # every account again
  agentbox claude-account myapp                       # show the account and the list
  ```
- **The list applies everywhere an account is chosen:** `agentbox create --claude-account`, the chat's `create_agent`, the New agent dialog, `agentbox claude-account <project/agent>`, forks and the project's own chat. An account outside the list is refused, and the error names the allowed ones. The project's own account has to be on its list, so AgentBox never quietly moves a project's billing to another account.
- **The chat sees only the allowed accounts.** `list_accounts` leaves the others out, and the chat's brief offers to spread agents across accounts only when more than one is allowed.

### Choose the context window per chat

- **A Context window control sits beside the model and the effort** in the project's chat and in every Claude Code agent's chat. It offers your installation's compact window, 200k by default, and the model's whole window, 1M for Opus and Sonnet. It is hidden when the two are the same, as they are for Haiku.
- **The window you choose is where that chat compacts.** In Claude Code that is what a context window actually changes: `opus` and `sonnet` already run with 1M, and adding `[1m]` to the name changes nothing. 200k stays the default because every step resends the whole conversation, so late in a long task a 1M chat can cost up to five times as much per step. The 1M choice says so.
- **A change mid-chat applies from your next message.** The chat says Claude Code will restart then. The next turn restarts it and resumes the same conversation, so nothing is lost.
- **Choose it when an agent is made:** `--context-window 1m` on `agentbox create`, `context_window` on the chat's `create_agent`, or a field in the New agent dialog. It is checked against the agent's model, so `1m` for Haiku is refused, and so is any window for a Codex or OpenCode agent. The agent's brief and its terminal's Claude Code settings use the window you chose.
- **The context meter, and the chat's rollover into a fresh session, measure against the chosen window**, not against the model's whole window.

### A terser project chat that gets on with it

- **Short answers:** a few sentences, the outcome first, headings and tables only when you ask for a plan or a comparison, one line for each agent it starts, and at most one question. It doesn't open with preamble or narrate what it is about to do. It doesn't talk about AgentBox or its tools unless you ask.
- **Short instructions to agents, too:** its tasks and `tell_agent` messages are a few direct lines.
- **It does the routine itself** in `ask` (see Upgrading above), and in `on` it also makes the product calls and tells you what it did. The app and `agentbox autonomy` describe the two settings to match.
- **Less in front of it:** its recap of the conversation no longer lists what was produced. When an agent finishes, the notice gives its pull request's state and asks the chat to do what follows and tell you in a line. The notices it gets and the results of its most common tools are shorter.
- **Measured:** the brief went from about 3,000 to about 2,600 tokens, and replies to typical requests from 421 to 220 words on average.

## Known limitations

- **A project whose own account is blank, so that it uses the machine's default, can be given a list that leaves that default out.** The list is saved, and the project's next agent is refused. The app shows a warning under the list when that happens.
- **Limiting a project's accounts doesn't move agents that already hold an account outside the list.** Recreate them to change it.
- **A context window chosen mid-chat takes effect only from the next message**, and changing it restarts Claude Code for that chat, which then resumes the conversation.
- **The context window is Claude Code's only.** Codex and OpenCode agents are refused one. There is no per-project default either: the installation's compact window applies unless each chat or agent chooses otherwise.
- **The context window hasn't been tried in an agent's chat inside a real Incus machine**, only in the project's chat, which runs the same code. An account whose model menu offers a `[1m]` variant of a model with a short window hasn't been tried either.
- **`ask` now retires merged agents and starts the next one without asking.** If you want every step proposed first, tell the project's chat so in its notes.
- **The project chat's shorter replies were measured without its MCP tools**, on Sonnet, over a few prompts: a real chat's replies may differ.
- **There is no SECURITY.md yet.** Report a vulnerability to the maintainer privately, as CONTRIBUTING.md says, not in a public issue.
- **macOS and Windows aren't shipped.** AgentBox still runs on Linux on x86_64 only.
- Everything else is unchanged from [0.15.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.15.0), [0.14.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.14.0), [0.13.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.13.0) and [0.3.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.3.0).
